title: PII exception intake and stakeholder orchestration framework
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: define a lightweight, scalable intake and prioritization framework for customer requests that ask Redwood to redact, retain/extend retention, export, or otherwise alter handling of PII and sensitive logging data. These requests are non-bug operational controls and often touch legal, security, and platform SLAs. Scope: intake form, automated scoring, stakeholder orchestration matrix, decision SLA targets, and minimum audit trail requirements. Out of scope for this ticket: implementation of the backend export pipeline and on-prem connector work (tracked in ENG-34421).
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing intake form template (Confluence + Support) exists with clear fields for request type, affected product, sample logs, compliance justification, desired outcome, and preferred SLA.
An automated scoring rubric that maps requests into three lanes (Standard, Elevated, Emergency) based on risk/urgency/scale and outputs an initial routing recommendation.

Stakeholder orchestration matrix with named owners for each lane (Support PM, Security reviewer, Legal SME, Eng on-call) and explicit SLA targets: Standard=10 business days, Elevated=3 business days, Emergency=24 hours.
Audit and handoff checklist created (what metadata to capture, evidence required, and legal signoffs) and linked to the Console's ticket metadata model.
Communication templates created for customer-facing responses at each stage (acknowledge, info-request, decision, remediation plan).
Metrics and instrumentation defined: time-to-first-ack, time-to-decision, fraction of requests escalated, and post-action verification success rate (target >95%).
comments: 2026-02-25 | Ava Patel: Created ticket after a spike of customer ask threads in #enterprise-support about ad-hoc retention/PII redaction. Early ask: unify intake and reduce back-and-forth with legal.

2026-03-02 | Noah Kim: Drafted intake form fields and initial scoring rubric. Preferred approach: automated pre-score + human review for Elevated/Emergency. Trade-off: manual reviews cost cycles but reduce risk of under-scrubbing.

2026-03-04 | Security (R. Huang): Recommended adding required samples (scrubbed) and a mandatory threat-model checklist for Elevated/Emergency lanes. Flagged potential integration with KMS audit logs.

2026-03-06 | Legal (S. Moore): Approved communication templates; requested explicit retention justification and customer legal contact in the intake form. Recommended retention justification taxonomy (Compliance/Business/Customer-request).

2026-03-08 | Noah Kim: Updated scoring rubric to include data volume buckets and PII sensitivity levels (low/medium/high) — see Confluence draft. Noted that extremely large-volume exports require ENG capacity coordination (dependency ENG-34421).

2026-03-10 | PM Review (A. Patel): Reviewed SLA targets with GTM and Support leads. Agreed to pilot Standard=10bd, Elevated=3bd, Emergency=24hr. Added metric gating to require average time-to-decision < SLA during 30-day pilot before roll out.

2026-03-11 | Design (L. Tran): Shared sample UI for intake on Console support panel (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/pii-intake-ui. Suggests progressive disclosure for sensitive fields to reduce user friction.

2026-03-12 | Noah Kim: Plan for next steps: finalize Confluence PR, build Support form + automation rule, create an internal Slack workflow for emergency lane notifications, and schedule cross-functional pilot with three enterprise customers. Assigned follow-ups to ENG and Security.
